problems.title: Naive Pattern Search

description.en: Given a text string and a pattern string, find all occurrences of the pattern in the text using the naive (brute force) approach. Print the starting index of each occurrence.
description.hi: Ek text string aur ek pattern string diya hai, naive (brute force) approach use karke text mein pattern ke saare occurrences dhundho. Har occurrence ka starting index print karo.

explanation.en: Pattern 'AABA' is found at indices 0, 9, and 12 in the text
explanation.hi: Pattern 'AABA' text mein indices 0, 9, aur 12 pe mila

explanation.en: Pattern 'XYZ' is not found anywhere in the text, so print -1
explanation.hi: Pattern 'XYZ' text mein kahin nahi mila, isliye -1 print karo

constraints: Both strings contain only uppercase English letters

hints.hi: Text ki har position i ke liye, pattern[0..m-1] ko text[i..i+m-1] se compare karo

problems.title: Rabin-Karp Search

description.en: Implement the Rabin-Karp algorithm to find all occurrences of a pattern in a given text. Use a rolling hash function with a prime modulus to efficiently compute hash values for sliding windows.
description.hi: Rabin-Karp algorithm implement karo text mein pattern ke saare occurrences dhundhne ke liye. Sliding windows ke liye efficiently hash values compute karne ke liye rolling hash function aur prime modulus use karo.

explanation.en: Pattern 'GEEK' is found at indices 0 and 10. The rolling hash allows O(1) hash update per window slide.
explanation.hi: Pattern 'GEEK' indices 0 aur 10 pe mila. Rolling hash har window slide ke liye O(1) hash update allow karta hai.

constraints: Both strings contain only printable ASCII characters

hints.en: Use d=256 (alphabet size) and a prime q for modular hashing. Compute h = d^(m-1) % q for the rolling hash.
hints.hi: d=256 (alphabet size) aur ek prime q modular hashing ke liye use karo. Rolling hash ke liye h = d^(m-1) % q compute karo.

hints.en: When hashes match, always verify by comparing characters to handle spurious hits (hash collisions).
hints.hi: Jab hashes match hon, hamesha characters compare karke verify karo spurious hits (hash collisions) handle karne ke liye.

problems.title: Shortest Palindrome

description.en: Given a string s, you can add characters in front of it to make it a palindrome. Find the shortest palindrome you can create by adding characters only to the front of the string.
description.hi: Ek string s diya hai, tum uske aage characters add karke isse palindrome bana sakte ho. String ke sirf aage characters add karke sabse chhota palindrome banao jo bana sakte ho.

explanation.en: Add 'a' to the front to make it a palindrome. The longest palindromic prefix is 'aacecaa', so we only need to add the reverse of remaining 'a' at the front.
explanation.hi: Aage 'a' add karo palindrome banane ke liye. Longest palindromic prefix 'aacecaa' hai, isliye sirf bache hue 'a' ka reverse aage add karna hai.

explanation.en: The longest palindromic prefix is just 'a'. Reverse of 'bcd' ('dcb') is added to the front.
explanation.hi: Longest palindromic prefix sirf 'a' hai. 'bcd' ka reverse ('dcb') aage add hota hai.

constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters

hints.en: The key insight is finding the longest palindromic prefix of the string. Characters after this prefix need to be reversed and prepended.
hints.hi: Key insight hai string ka longest palindromic prefix dhundhna. Is prefix ke baad ke characters ko reverse karke prepend karna hai.

hints.en: Use KMP: Create string = s + '#' + reverse(s), build LPS array. The last value of LPS gives the longest palindromic prefix length.
hints.hi: KMP use karo: string = s + '#' + reverse(s) banao, LPS array banao. LPS ki last value longest palindromic prefix ki length deti hai.

approach.en: Use KMP's LPS array on s + '#' + reverse(s). The last LPS value gives the longest palindromic prefix. Reverse the remaining suffix and prepend it to s.
approach.hi: s + '#' + reverse(s) pe KMP ka LPS array use karo. Last LPS value longest palindromic prefix deta hai. Bache hue suffix ko reverse karke s ke aage lagao.

code.python:
def shortest_palindrome(s):
    if not s: return s
    rev = s[::-1]
    concat = s + '#' + rev
    n = len(concat)
    lps = [0] * n
    length = 0; i = 1
    while i < n:
        if concat[i] == concat[length]:
            length += 1; lps[i] = length; i += 1
        else:
            if length: length = lps[length-1]
            else: lps[i] = 0; i += 1
    return rev[:len(s) - lps[-1]] + s

problems.title: Repeated String Match

description.en: Given two strings a and b, return the minimum number of times string a must be repeated such that string b is a substring of the repeated string. If b can never be a substring of a repeated a, return -1.
description.hi: Do strings a aur b diye hain, string a ko minimum kitni baar repeat karna padega taaki string b repeated string ka substring ban jaaye wo return karo. Agar b kabhi bhi repeated a ka substring nahi ban sakta, to -1 return karo.

explanation.en: Repeat a 3 times: 'abcdabcdabcd'. Now b = 'cdabcdab' is a substring of this repeated string.
explanation.hi: a ko 3 baar repeat karo: 'abcdabcdabcd'. Ab b = 'cdabcdab' is repeated string ka substring hai.

explanation.en: Repeat a 4 times: 'abcabcabcabc'. Now b = 'cabcabca' is found as a substring.
explanation.hi: a ko 4 baar repeat karo: 'abcabcabcabc'. Ab b = 'cabcabca' substring ke roop mein mil gaya.

constraints: a and b consist of lowercase English letters

hints.en: The maximum number of repetitions needed is ceil(len(b)/len(a)) + 1. If b is not found by then, it will never be found.
hints.hi: Maximum repetitions jo chahiye hain wo ceil(len(b)/len(a)) + 1 hain. Agar tab tak b na mile, to kabhi nahi milega.

hints.en: Repeat a enough times so the repeated string is at least as long as b, then check once more. Use KMP or Rabin-Karp for efficient substring check.
hints.hi: a ko itni baar repeat karo ki repeated string kam se kam b jitni lambi ho, phir ek baar aur check karo. Efficient substring check ke liye KMP ya Rabin-Karp use karo.

problems.title: Longest Happy Prefix

description.en: A string is called a happy prefix if it is a non-empty prefix which is also a suffix (excluding the entire string itself). Given a string s, find the longest happy prefix of s. Return an empty string if no such prefix exists.
description.hi: Ek string ko happy prefix tab kehte hain jab wo ek non-empty prefix ho jo suffix bhi ho (poori string ko chhodke). Ek string s diya hai, s ka longest happy prefix dhundho. Agar aisa koi prefix na ho to empty string return karo.

explanation.en: The prefixes that are also suffixes are: 'l'. So 'l' is the longest happy prefix with length 1.
explanation.hi: Jo prefixes suffix bhi hain wo hain: 'l'. Isliye 'l' longest happy prefix hai length 1 ke saath.

explanation.en: 'ab' and 'abab' are both prefixes that are also suffixes. 'abab' is the longest with length 4.
explanation.hi: 'ab' aur 'abab' dono prefixes hain jo suffix bhi hain. 'abab' longest hai length 4 ke saath.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters

hints.en: This is exactly what the KMP's LPS (Failure Function) array computes! The last value of the LPS array gives the answer.
hints.hi: Yehi to KMP ka LPS (Failure Function) array compute karta hai! LPS array ki last value answer deti hai.

hints.en: You can also use the Z-algorithm: check Z[i] values where i + Z[i] == n (the match extends to the end).
hints.hi: Z-algorithm bhi use kar sakte ho: Z[i] values check karo jahan i + Z[i] == n (match end tak extend hota hai).
